The major thyroid hormone made by the thyroid gland is thyroxine, called T4. The thyroid makes a smaller amount of triiodothyronine (T3), but most of the body’s T3 comes from conversion of T4 to T3 outside of the thyroid. The production of thyroid hormones is controlled by thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), which is made in the pituitary gland near the brain. The pituitary is always measuring the amount of thyroid hormone and adjusts the amount of TSH in order to “talk” to the thyroid. If there is less T4, TSH will go up to tell the thyroid gland to produce more, and vice versa. By listening to each other, TSH and T4 keep each other balanced in a fairly narrow range. The thyroid makes a smaller amount of triiodothyronine (T3), but most of the body’s T3 comes from conversion of T4 to T3 outside of the thyroid. chunks.text: The major thyroid hormone made by the thyroid gland is thyroxine, called T4. The thyroid makes a smaller amount of triiodothyronine (T3), but most of the body’s T3 comes from conversion of T4 to T3 outside of the thyroid. The production of thyroid hormones is controlled by thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), which is made in the pituitary gland near the brain. The pituitary is always measuring the amount of thyroid hormone and adjusts the amount of TSH in order to “talk” to the thyroid. If there is less T4, TSH will go up to tell the thyroid gland to produce more, and vice versa. By listening to each other, TSH and T4 keep each other balanced in a fairly narrow range. Thyroid hormones are released into the blood and carried to every tissue in the body. The major thyroid hormone made by the thyroid gland is thyroxine, called T4. The thyroid makes a smaller amount of triiodothyronine (T3), but most of the body’s T3 comes from conversion of T4 to T3 outside of the thyroid. The production of thyroid hormones is controlled by thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), which is made in the pituitary gland near the brain. The pituitary is always measuring the amount of thyroid hormone and adjusts the amount of TSH in order to “talk” to the thyroid. If there is less T4, TSH will go up to tell the thyroid gland to produce more, and vice versa. By listening to each other, TSH and T4 keep each other balanced in a fairly narrow range.
